declared_purpose: Generate standard, editable PPTX presentations from JSON, supporting styled slides, tables, charts, timelines, images, contact information, footers and page numbers. Per-slide error skipping and reporting are explicit features (SKILL.md:3-17,20-62,87-92). Filesystem handling and diagnostic payloads are implementation choices.

data_operations.source: File selected by the first CLI argument
data_operations.data_scope: Entire JSON document, including fields subsequently unused by rendering
data_operations.condition: Normal CLI generation after the help branch; this file read is not performed by build_from_json itself.

data_operations.operation: Construct editable presentation content and return the generator
data_operations.source: Supplied JSON object or direct method arguments
data_operations.data_scope: Slide text, lists, tables, author/date, quotations and attribution, contact information, milestones, footer and presentation settings. These are supplied content, not inferred personal attributes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-memory python-pptx presentation; build_from_json returns the generator to its caller
data_operations.condition: Recognized slide types are dispatched to their applicable methods. Returning the generator does not itself save or remotely disclose it.

data_operations.operation: Supply chart data and request derived percentage labels
data_operations.data_scope: Supplied chart data; percentage labels requested for pie charts
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CategoryChartData and the in-memory presentation through python-pptx
data_operations.condition: Chart slides use the later, effective add_chart definition; pie charts enable percentage labels. Earlier duplicate definitions do not execute additionally.

data_operations.operation: Check an image file and request its insertion
data_operations.data_scope: Selected file's existence and image content, plus supplied title/caption
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Filesystem check and python-pptx picture insertion into the presentation
data_operations.condition: Image slides only. Validation precedes slide creation. With overlay=true, a solid full-slide shape is placed over the inserted image; the code does not remove that picture.

data_operations.data_scope: Rendered slide content and inserted media; partially constructed slides can also remain after caught rendering errors
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Filesystem destination selected by --out, otherwise JSON output, otherwise output.pptx
data_operations.condition: CLI generation reaches save. Per-slide exceptions are caught without removing slides already added, so later saving can include their partial content.

data_operations.source: Slide description and caught rendering exception
data_operations.data_scope: Slide index/total, full title, type and exception string; a missing-image exception includes image_path
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard error, available to the invoking caller
data_operations.condition: A slide renderer raises an exception caught by build_from_json. No remote recipient or durable logging destination is specified.

data_operations.operation: Return CLI completion information or top-level errors
data_operations.source: Output selection, generator page counter and uncaught exceptions
data_operations.data_scope: Output path and page count on success; exception text on failure
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output or standard error to the invoking caller
data_operations.condition: Successful save emits completion information; top-level failures emit diagnostics and exit with status 1. These streams do not establish external disclosure or persistence.

potential_excess.data_scope: Content already inserted into a slide whose rendering subsequently fails
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Saved PPTX at the selected output path
potential_excess.condition: An exception occurs after slide creation or partial population. For example, table rendering can fail while indexing a cell after earlier cells have been populated.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document promises error skipping and per-slide reports. Retaining partial content from a reported skipped slide is not required for that outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Save successfully generated slides and report unsuccessful ones.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make slide construction transactional, removing failed slides and their associated content before saving.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve successful slides, accurate page numbering and failure reports. This narrows artifact contents; it does not require another output artifact or deletion of input files.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full slide titles and raw exception details, including image paths on validation failure
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Per-slide standard-error diagnostic payload delivered to the caller
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Per-slide reporting is explicit; echoing complete user text and raw filesystem paths is a formatting choice. This is extra data within a required report, not a redundant reporting action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the failed slide and provide an actionable error category.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Default to slide index/total, type and a concise error category; provide full titles and path-bearing details only when detailed diagnostics are requested.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain useful failure identification and troubleshooting. No broader recipient or downstream log retention is established by the supplied source.

unknowns: python-pptx and its dependencies are not supplied. Exact image-byte retention, image metadata, chart backing data, default presentation metadata and dependency side effects remain unresolved.
Filesystem paths are caller-controlled; the source does not establish whether their backing storage is local, shared or remotely mounted.
Caller handling of returned objects, output files and diagnostic streams is unspecified, including access, subsequent disclosure, retention and deletion.
The supplied-source audit is complete; dependency internals and downstream handling cannot be determined from this package.
